rules.statement: A CI workflow whose job reports a required status check must trigger on `merge_group` events and on pushes to and pull requests into the release branches (`release/**`), not just on pull requests into `main`.
rules.why: A required check whose workflow never runs stays pending forever, so the merge queue and release-line pull requests would wait on it indefinitely.
rules.check: In a new or changed `.github/workflows/*.yml` that produces a required check, confirm the `on:` block has `merge_group` plus `push` and `pull_request` for `release/**`, and that no path filter or job condition skips the job on those events.

rules.statement: When a change adds a file that affects the whole build (for example a new `Directory.*` file, `BannedSymbols*.txt`, `.runsettings`, SDK or NuGet config, or a file under `build/` or `.config/`), add it to the global-input trigger pattern of the affected-tests selector so that changing it runs every test.
rules.why: If a global build input is missing from the pattern, a pull request runs too few tests and only the merge queue's full gate catches the break.
rules.check: Look for new repository-wide build inputs in the diff that are not added to the global trigger pattern in `build/affected-tests.ps1`.

rules.statement: Skip coverage uploads (such as Codecov) on `merge_group` runs, because the push to `main` already uploads coverage for the same merged result.
rules.why: The merge queue's run would upload the same coverage that `main`'s push uploads.
rules.check: In a CI workflow, a coverage upload step that has no `if: github.event_name != 'merge_group'` (or an equivalent condition).
